images.note: Contemporary (1950). Shows the South Korean retreat in the invasion's opening days at Suwon Airfield, just south of Seoul; the caption explicitly references North Korea's Soviet-built T-34/85 tanks, matching the script's 'tanks in the lead' beat. DoD photo republished by Defense Media Network. Alt: none qualifying — the only other 1950 retreat image found (DVIDS 5836383, UN troops outside Seoul, Sept 1950) is 800px wide.
images.source: U.S. Department of Defense (via Defense Media Network)
images.title: South Korean evacuation of Suwon Airfield, 1950

images.note: Contemporary (July 11, 1950). U.S. Army infantry engaging the North Korean invasion in the same first weeks as Task Force Smith's July 5 stand at Osan. Honest limitation: this is not Task Force Smith itself — no verified Task Force Smith combat photograph was found at the 1200px bar (DVIDS holds only modern memorial-ceremony photos). U.S. Army photo republished by Defense Media Network. Alt: none at bar from a second institution.
images.title: American mortar crew fires on North Korean invaders, Chochiwan, July 1950

images.note: Contemporary (July 18, 1950). Soldiers of the 24th Infantry Regiment — Task Force Smith was drawn from the 24th Infantry Division, so this is the closest verified unit match for the 'first Americans in' beat. U.S. Army photo republished by Defense Media Network. Alt: none at bar from a second institution.
images.title: 24th Infantry Regiment moves to the firing line, Korea, July 1950

images.note: Contemporary (August 26, 1950). Machine-gun squad firing on North Korean patrols along the north bank of the Naktong River — the Naktong line was the backbone of the Pusan perimeter. U.S. Army photo republished by Defense Media Network. Alt: none qualifying — no second-institution Pusan-perimeter period photo found at the 1200px bar.
images.title: Firefight on the Naktong River line, August 1950

images.note: Contemporary (early November 1950). 7th Regiment, 1st Marine Division pushing through snow toward the Chosin Reservoir in North Korea — the drive-north phase weeks before China's late-November intervention. DoD photo via war.gov on DVIDS, public domain. Alt: none at bar from a second institution.
images.source: U.S. Department of Defense (via DVIDS / war.gov)
images.title: Marines push toward the Chosin Reservoir, North Korea, November 1950

images.note: Both contemporary (December 1950). Primary: Marines of the 5th and 7th Regiments awaiting withdrawal as Chinese divisions close in — National Archives photo via DVIDS. Alt: 1st Marine Division members passing destroyed equipment during the breakout, Dec 7, 1950, DoD photo by Sgt. F.C. Kerr, USMC via war.gov. Different images, different source institutions (National Archives vs. U.S. Marine Corps); both files served via the DVIDS CloudFront CDN, so a CDN outage would affect both — flagged for the pipeline.
images.title: Marines await withdrawal, Chosin Reservoir area, December 1950

images.note: Contemporary (December 13, 1950). Honors team of the 1st Marine Division firing a volley at the division cemetery at Hungnam after the Chosin breakout. Serves the verdict beat ('around forty thousand American dead... the Forgotten War'). Honest limitation: this is a 1950 field memorial service, NOT the 1995 Korean War Veterans Memorial — no verified photograph of the 1995 memorial was found at the bar. DoD photo by Cpl. W.T. Wolfe, USMC via war.gov on DVIDS, public domain. Alt: none at bar from a second institution.
images.title: Memorial service for the fallen after the Chosin breakout, Hungnam, December 1950
